# Recipient remove-wins across a merge: ours revokes a recipient key that theirs
# removes and then re-adds. The re-add must not resurrect the revoked key, so the
# revoked identity stays locked out after the merge.

sesam-repo

# bob has two recipient keys; carol's key can decrypt the log via bob.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob with two keys'
exec sesam --identity $CAROL_KEY show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl

# OURS revokes carol's key.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user remove-recipient --user bob --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: revoke carol key'

# THEIRS revokes then re-adds carol's key (net: still present on theirs).
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user remove-recipient --user bob --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY
exec sesam user add-recipient --user bob --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: churn carol key'

exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
exec git commit --no-edit

# Remove wins: theirs' re-add was dropped, so carol stays locked out.
exec sesam verify
! exec sesam --identity $CAROL_KEY show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
